title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model
authors: Y. Bengio, R. Ducharme, P. Vincent, C. Jauvin
before: Language models counted discrete n-grams, with smoothing to patch the gaps.
problem: The curse of dimensionality: the number of possible word sequences grows faster than any corpus can cover.
breakthrough: Learn a continuous vector per word jointly with the language model, so unseen sequences inherit probability from similar ones.
why: The first model where meaning lives in learned geometry. Every embedding layer in every LLM descends from this.
next: Word2vec made these vectors cheap enough to compute at scale.
inherits: Distributed word representations trained by next-word prediction.
